title: How do the planet and its axle move?
description: Distinguish the planet's frame-relative spin from its axle's orbit around a locked sun.
question: Drive H CCW in the front view. Find P (frame spin) and H (carried-axle orbit) at the shown instant.

answer.explanation: Drive H CCW. External mesh S/P (24/16 teeth) uses spins relative to carrier H. S held, P negative. S is locked to the frame. S held. 24 × (S − H) + 16 × (P − H) = 0. The requested motion is CCW / CCW (in listed output order).

options.label: A
options.explanation: P is CCW, while this choice gives stationary. A stationary point at tooth contact allows the planet body to spin while its center orbits.

options.label: B
options.explanation: H is CCW, while this choice gives CW. The axle rides on H and follows its prescribed CCW orbit.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This tuple matches the derived motions. The fixed sun appears CW on H. The external planet spins CCW on H. Adding the CCW carrier gives CCW frame spin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: P is CCW, while this choice gives CW. The carrier does turn CCW. Treating the fixed sun as a frame-mounted driving gear reverses the planet incorrectly.
